content: Each interaction is described individually, maintaining the original level of detail. 1. Cephalexin and Meloxicam: Cephalexin may increase the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of meloxicam due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Cephalexin and Mesalamine: Cephalexin may elevate the levels or effects of mesalamine through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical relevance of this interaction remains uncertain. 3. Cephalexin and Methyclothiazide: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of methyclothiazide by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well established. 4. Cephalexin and Metolazone: Cephalexin may enhance the levels or effects of metolazone via competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical importance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Cephalexin and Nabumetone: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of nabumetone due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 6. Cephalexin and Naproxen: Cephalexin may elevate the levels or effects of naproxen by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical relevance of this interaction is uncertain. 7. Cephalexin and Oxaprozin: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of oxaprozin through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well defined. 8. Cephalexin and Pantothenic Acid: Cephalexin may reduce the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 9. Cephalexin and Parecoxib: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of parecoxib due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical importance of this interaction is uncertain. 10. Cephalexin and Patiromer: Cephalexin may interact with patiromer through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. No clinically significant interaction has been observed, and no separation of dosing is required. 11. Cephalexin and Piroxicam: Cephalexin may elevate the levels or effects of piroxicam by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Cephalexin and Pyridoxine: Cephalexin may decrease the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical relevance is uncertain. 13. Cephalexin and Rose Hips: Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of cephalexin through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 14. Cephalexin and Salicylates (Non-ASA): Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of non-aspirin salicylates by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical importance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Cephalexin and Salsalate: Cephalexin may elevate the levels or effects of salsalate due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 16. Cephalexin and Sulfasalazine: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of sulfasalazine by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Cephalexin and Sulindac: Cephalexin may enhance the levels or effects of sulindac through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 18. Cephalexin and Thiamine: Cephalexin may reduce the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical importance is uncertain. 19. Cephalexin and Tolfenamic Acid: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of tolfenamic acid due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Cephalexin and Tolmetin: Cephalexin may elevate the levels or effects of tolmetin by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical relevance of this interaction is uncertain. 21. Cephalexin and Valganciclovir: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of valganciclovir through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 22. Cephalexin and Willow Bark: Cephalexin may enhance the levels or effects of willow bark by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical importance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Cephalexin and Acyclovir: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of acyclovir due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 24. Cephalexin and Amikacin: Cephalexin may increase the nephrotoxic and/or ototoxic effects of amikacin. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 25. Cephalexin and Aminohippurate Sodium: Cephalexin may elevate the levels or effects of aminohippurate sodium by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Cephalexin and Aspirin: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of aspirin through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical relevance of this interaction is uncertain. 27. Cephalexin and Aspirin Rectal: Cephalexin may enhance the levels or effects of rectal aspirin by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Cephalexin and Aspirin/Citric Acid/Sodium Bicarbonate: Cephalexin may increase the levels or effects of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical importance of this interaction is unclear. 29. Cephalexin and Atezolizumab: Cephalexin may reduce the therapeutic effects of atezolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, as coadministration may interfere with the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 30. Cephalexin and Avelumab: Cephalexin may decrease the therapeutic effects of avelumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised, as coadministration may interfere with the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors.
